lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Performance task planning: interpreting probability results in context

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows how to justify a modelling choice.

items.prompt: P(A and B) = 3/20, P(B) = 5/20. Find P(A|B).

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Decide what the quantities are before you compute anything.

items.prompt: Given P(A) = 2/20, P(B) = 4/20, and P(A and B) = 1/20, find P(A or B) in lowest terms.
In a study, P(passes | attended the workshop) is higher than P(passes) overall. What is the correct interpretation?
choices: The two events are mutually exclusive.
The two conditional probabilities are equal, so the order of conditioning never matters.
The relationship proves that one event causes the other.
Attendance and passing are associated, though this alone does not show that the workshop caused the improvement.

items.prompt: A box holds 17 items, of which 8 are defective. Two are drawn without replacement. Find the probability that both are defective, in lowest terms.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Plan in writing: what you will model, why that model, and how you will check it.

items.prompt: Given P(A and B) = 87/100 and P(B) = 88/100, find P(A | B) as a fraction in lowest terms.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: Given P(A) = 33/100, P(B) = 16/100, and P(A and B) = 13/100, find P(A or B) in lowest terms.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: In a study, P(has the condition | tested positive) is much smaller than P(tested positive | has the condition). What is the correct interpretation?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
